entries.title: Selecting text highlights it
entries.body: In an article you own, selecting text with the mouse highlights it in yellow and opens a box for adding a comment. Click away to keep the highlight, or choose Remove highlight. If you only wanted the words, Copy, don't highlight copies them and takes the highlight off again. On a touch screen, Highlight or comment does the same. Referee works as before. Saving takes a moment, so a highlight made just before you reload the page may not be kept.

entries.title: Brief can be read while Fuller is written
entries.body: When Summary is written for one of your articles for the first time, you can read Brief as soon as it is finished, while Fuller is still being written. Fuller is longer than it was: the AI is asked for five to eight paragraphs and about 500 words. A middle level that was written but never shown is gone.

entries.title: Find more adds to the glossary you have
entries.body: In Glossary, Find more adds terms to the list you already have instead of replacing it. When the list has to be replaced, because the article or your profile has changed or the saved list is too old to add to, the button reads Write a new list and says why. If nothing more turns up, it tells you so.

entries.title: Remember's four buttons explain themselves
entries.body: Point at any of Remember's four buttons and a card says what it does. The information card in Recall, Tutorial and Explore is two sentences and a short list rather than one long paragraph. Results written for you are marked with a small person icon: point at it for an explanation, or press it to open your profile.

entries.title: Search boxes have a cross to empty them
entries.body: The search box in your library has a larger, clearer cross for emptying it, and Escape empties it too. The Quick search box in the bar at the bottom of an article has one as well, shown while the box has text. Pressing it leaves the cursor in the box, ready for the next search.

entries.title: Two causes of failed large imports are fixed
entries.body: Adding a very long article could fail with a message asking you to try again, and trying again failed the same way. A PDF with unusually heavy pages could be refused although it could have been read. Both are fixed. Some oversized PDFs are still refused.

entries.title: Copy buttons show your latest press's result
entries.body: If you pressed a copy button more than once, a slow earlier attempt could show a failure although the text had been copied, or the tick could vanish early. Copy buttons across the app show the outcome of the latest press. In your library, a Copy link that fails and then works no longer leaves the failure message showing.

entries.title: Cards and panels no longer open off-screen
entries.body: On a phone, tapping a row in Structure's list could open its card off the right edge and shift the page; the card can drop below the row instead. On a narrow window, Open glossary and Dig deeper could leave the panel hidden; they bring it back. And a panel's (i) card no longer reopens after two quick presses.
